chunks: And among what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from al-Sindī ibn Muḥammad al-Bazzāz, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a woman who sees blood for five days and purity for five days, then sees blood for four days and purity for six days. He said: If she sees blood, she does not perform salat; and if she sees purity, she performs salat during the period between that and thirty days. Then when thirty days are completed, if she sees flowing blood, she performs ghusl, fastens her cloth, and uses cotton at the time of every salat; and if she sees yellowish discharge, she performs wudu (ablution).

The proper way regarding these two reports is that we carry them upon a woman whose habit in menstruation has become confused and changed from its times, and likewise the days of her cycles, and the quality of the blood has become unclear to her, so that the blood of menstruation is not distinguishable for her from other than it.
For if that is the case, then her obligation, when she sees blood, is to leave salat, and when she sees purity, she performs salat until she comes to know her habit.

And it is also possible that this is the ruling of a woman in istihadah whose menstrual days have become confused for her, whose habit has changed, and whose bleeding has continued, while the quality of the blood is ambiguous; so she sees what resembles menstrual blood for three or four days, and she sees what resembles the blood of istihadah likewise, and she has not attained knowledge of which one of the two it is.

Then her obligation is to leave salat whenever she sees what resembles menstrual blood, and to perform salat whenever she sees what resembles the blood of istihadah, for up to a month; then after that she does what a woman in istihadah does.

And his statement, 'she saw purity for three or four days,' may mean what resembles the blood of istihadah, because istihadah is under the ruling of purity. For that reason he said in the report, 'then she does what a woman in istihadah does,' and that only occurs along with continuing blood. This is indicated by the report that we have cited in our larger book from more than one person who asked Abā ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about menstruation and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) concerning it.

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood, here referring to bleeding relevant to menstrual rulings
key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: the transmitted normative practice concerning the matter
key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: ritual purity or the interval of cleanliness in which salat is performed
key_terms.الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ: non-menstrual irregular bleeding treated under separate legal rulings
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation with its specific legal consequences
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفِ: cotton used by the woman to manage bleeding

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who has irregular bleeding and cannot distinguish menstruation from istihadah?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of a woman whose bleeding pattern has become irregular and whose usual menstrual habit is no longer clear. It explains that she leaves salat when she sees what appears to be menstrual blood and performs salat when she sees purity or what resembles istihadah, until her pattern becomes known or until she follows the rulings of istihadah after a month.
